simple.meaning: פָּצַע (pâtsaʻ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to split , i.e. wound.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Song of Solomon, beginning at Deuteronomy 23:2. Its contexts include birth, family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּצַע (H6481).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: פָּצַע (pâtsaʻ) / H6481 is traced through Deuteronomy 23:2, 1 Kings 20:37, Song of Songs 5:7 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H6481. patsa [ מָּצַע ] verb bruise, wound by bruising (Late Hebrew split, bruise ; Arabic squeeze a ripe date, rub ; Aramaic מְּצַע split ); — Qal Perfect 3plural suffix מְּצָעוּנִי הִכּוּנִי Song 5:7 ; Infinitive absolute וּפָצֹעַ הַכֵּה 1Kin 20:37 a smiting and a bruising (him); Participle Pass. construct מְּצוּעַדַּֿכָּה Deut 23:2 one wounded by crushing.

occurrences.englishText: A person born of a forbidden union shall not enter into Yahweh’s assembly; even to the tenth generation shall no one of his enter into Yahweh’s assembly.
Then he found another man, and said, “Please strike me.”
